entries.title: Adult Activity: An Overview
entries.organisation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
entries.license: U.S. federal government public-domain text, unless otherwise noted
entries.content: CDC guidance says adults should aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity each week, or an equivalent amount of vigorous or mixed activity, and should do muscle-strengthening activity on at least 2 days each week. Activity can be spread across the week and broken into smaller amounts; some activity is better than none.

entries.title: About Sleep
entries.organisation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
entries.license: U.S. federal government public-domain text, unless otherwise noted
entries.content: CDC sleep guidance recommends consistent bed and wake times, a quiet and relaxing bedroom at a cool temperature, turning off electronic devices before bedtime, avoiding large meals and alcohol before bed, limiting caffeine later in the day, and exercising regularly. Adults ages 18 to 60 generally need 7 or more hours of sleep per day.

entries.title: About Sleep
entries.organisation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
entries.license: U.S. federal government public-domain text, unless otherwise noted
entries.content: CDC advises talking with a healthcare provider when sleep problems occur regularly or when there are signs or symptoms of a sleep disorder. A clinician may use a sleep diary or other evaluation to understand persistent sleep problems.

entries.title: Managing Stress
entries.section_title: Healthy ways to cope with stress
entries.organisation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
entries.license: U.S. federal government public-domain text, unless otherwise noted
entries.content: CDC describes occasional stress as a normal part of life and notes that long-term stress can worsen health problems. Healthy coping can include small daily steps, recognizing triggers, taking breaks from distressing news or social media, and seeking additional support when it is difficult to cope.

entries.title: Preventing Falls and Hip Fractures
entries.section_title: Preventing a fall or hip fracture
entries.organisation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
entries.license: U.S. federal government public-domain text, unless otherwise noted
entries.content: CDC fall-prevention guidance recommends discussing fall risk with a healthcare provider, reviewing medicines that may cause dizziness or sleepiness, doing exercises that improve leg strength and balance, keeping vision care up to date, and reducing tripping hazards while improving lighting and supports at home.
